title: Diagnostic: Make switch Exhaustive
hints: A `switch` over an enum must cover every case — unless there's a `default`.
Remove the `default` and list only three of the four cases.
Cases `.sun`, `.rain` and `.wind` only — leave `.snow` out and drop `default`.
jsBridge: TS's `never` exhaustiveness check (`const _: never = x`) is opt-in. Swift makes exhaustiveness **mandatory** for `switch` over enums, which is why adding a case breaks every switch that doesn't handle it. That's usually what you want.

compass.q: In TS you add `default: assertNever(x)` to get this. What's the cost of Swift doing it by default?
What is `@unknown default`, and why do switches over Apple's enums (`UIUserInterfaceStyle`) need it?
You add `case snow` to an enum used in 40 places. Is "breaking the build" good or bad? When would `default` be the right call?
Java 21's switch patterns over sealed types are exhaustive too. How do Swift enums compare with sealed interfaces?
